bayDoors.source: ESTIMATE (D1, 2026-10-09): travel time and drag area by analogy with the G4M's (0.36 sq m for an opening of about 2.4 sq m), scaled to this bay's 4.3 x 0.66 m opening. Nothing measured; both are tuning values.

combat.source: Armament: two fixed .50 in wing guns (EN-WP 'Grumman TBF Avenger', Armament: 'two 0.50 in wing guns' on later models; HOW: 'two fixed forward-firing 0.50in guns'). 600 rounds per gun is an ESTIMATE (no source read gives the count). The .50's ballistics are the fleet's top-level ones, copied from the F6F's combat block (800 rpm, 883.92 m/s, dragPerM 0.00015), as every .50 in the fleet. The dorsal ball turret's .50 and the ventral .30 are drawn and AIM (Turret1 and Turret2, turret aim and flex guns) but do NOT fire: defensive gunners are Track E3 (D11, Mark, 2026-10-09). Gun positions: 3.6 m out on each wing, just ahead of the leading edge, measured on the drawn model. Hit zones follow the drawn airframe (combatFit.test.ts); structureHp 140 and subsystemHp 45 are ESTIMATES, above the F6F's 120 and 40 for a larger, famously rugged airplane; the rest of the block is the F6F's. Damage stages round 2 (Mark, 2026-10-10, on merging with D1): structureHp and subsystemHp are 4x the values above, as for every fighter (docs/handoff/2026-10-09-aircraft-damage-stages.md, Round 2).

reference.source: Sources (all read 2026-10-09). NO FLIGHT-TEST REPORT OR PILOT'S HANDBOOK CHART WAS READ: wwiiaircraftperformance.org has no Avenger file, and the TBM-3 Pilot's Handbook (AN 01-190EB-1, 1 Nov 1945) is listed by sellers and file hosts but no copy could be fetched, so EVERY figure below is SECONDARY or an ESTIMATE (D10: primary first, else secondary, with the gap named). EN-WP = English Wikipedia 'Grumman TBF Avenger', Specifications (the TBF-1's block, citing Jane's Fighting Aircraft of World War II pp. 234-235); HOW = J. Rickard, 'Eastern TBM-3E Avenger', historyofwar.org (the TBM-3E's statistics, no bibliography). The TBM-3E shares the TBM-3's engine and airframe and is 300 lb lighter empty and 2,600 lb lighter loaded (HOW). Geometry: wingSpanM 16.51 = 54 ft 2 in and wingAreaM2 45.52 = 490 sq ft (EN-WP); the drawn model's length is HOW's 40 ft 11.5 in. Engine: one Wright R-2600-20, 1,900 hp (HOW), maxPowerW 1,416,830 = 1,900 x 745.7. powerFractionByAltitudeM is an ESTIMATE throughout (0.90 to 5,000 ft, 0.80 at 12,000 ft, 0.72 at 16,500 ft, 0.50 at 25,000 ft, 0.38 at 30,000 ft): no R-2600-20 altitude rating was read, and the 16,500 ft point is where the top speed is quoted. Mass: emptyKg 4,919 = 10,845 lb, DERIVED as HOW's TBM-3E empty 10,545 lb + 300 lb; fuelCapacityKg 898 = 330 US gal x 6 lb/gal (EN-WP's internal tanks; 6 lb/gal an ESTIMATE); maxTakeoffKg 8,117 = 17,895 lb, HOW's TBM-3E maximum (SECONDARY; the TBM-3's own is not read). testMassKg 6,423 = 14,160 lb, HOW's TBM-3E normal loaded weight: an ESTIMATE for pairing, because no source ties a weight to its speed or climb; the -3E figures are graded at the -3E's own loaded weight. It is 1,504 kg above emptyKg, which the harness carries as disposable load (crew, oil, ammunition and fuel; more than the 898 kg of fuel alone). Graded figures (SECONDARY, the TBM-3E's): topSpeedMps 123.4 = 276 mph at topSpeedAltitudeM 5,029 m = 16,500 ft (HOW); climbRateMps 10.47 = 2,060 ft/min initial, taken at sea level (HOW). EN-WP's 278 mph and 1,075 ft/min are the lighter, less powerful TBF-1's and are not used. Stalls: NONE SOURCED. stallSpeedMps 40.2 (90 mph) is an ESTIMATE, the speed at which the fleet's shared clMax 1.4 stalls testMassKg on 45.52 sq m, sqrt(2 x 6,423 x 9.81 / (1.225 x 45.52 x 1.4)): the card grades the model against its own estimate. stallSpeedFlapMps 34.5 is an ESTIMATE from flap.clIncrement 0.5 (also an ESTIMATE), so the flap card is circular too. FITTED, NOT SOURCED (measured 2026-10-09, a tools/testcards/measure.ts sweep at testMassKg, cd0 0.015 to 0.019 x propEfficiency 0.62 to 0.71): aero.cd0 0.019 and engine.propEfficiency 0.70 land the top speed -0.18 percent and the climb +0.38 percent; two unknowns to two secondary figures through an estimated power curve, so the fit proves nothing about either. Result (measured 2026-10-09): top speed 123.18 vs 123.4 m/s at 5,029 m; climb 10.51 vs 10.47 m/s at sea level; stalls 40.07 clean and 34.32 flaps against their own estimates; roll 45.0 vs its ESTIMATE. The model reads 115.4 m/s (258 mph) at sea level; no source was read to check it. engine.staticThrustN 19,000 is DERIVED, the Corsair's 20,000 N scaled by take-off power (1,417 / 1,491 kW); engine.windmillCd0 0.038 is DERIVED as 2 x cd0; negativeGCutout true (a float-carburetor Wright, ESTIMATE). gear.dragAreaM2 0.35 and flap.dragAreaM2 0.86 are ESTIMATES, the B-17's derived figures (1.20 and 2.94) scaled by wing area (45.52 / 131.92) and rounded; gear.travelSeconds 8 and flap.travelSeconds 6 are ESTIMATES. No take-off distance, roll rate, dive limit or g limit was read, so reference.takeoffDistanceM is absent and these are ESTIMATES: rollRateDegPerSec 45 (rates.maxRollRateDegPerSec is set to it), maxPitchRateDegPerSec 25, maxYawRateDegPerSec 12, limits.diveSpeedMps 155 (347 mph) and gLimit 5.0. The lift curve, rateRefSpeedMps, weathercockSeconds, autoRudderGainPerDeg and stallLimiterSeconds are the fleet's shared ESTIMATES. Gear layout (measured 2026-10-09 from the drawn model with a throwaway drawnPoints probe, the propeller excluded): the origin is the wing root's quarter chord; heightM 1.985 and mainX 0.250 (the mains' lowest point), thirdX -7.082 and thirdHeightM 0.711 (the fixed tailwheel, the first aft point to touch when pitched about the mains, 9.853 degrees). No TBM ground angle was read. layout taildragger and thirdSteering casterLock (the TBF's tailwheel locked for carrier work, ESTIMATE); steerYawRateDegPerSec 5, steerLockSpeedMps 8, tailLiftSpeedMps 26 and propWashSpeedMps 10 are ESTIMATES; torqueYawRateDegPerSec 0 (Mark's fleet ruling of 2026-09-28). carrierCapable true (the Avenger flew from fleet and escort carriers, EN-WP). view.eyePointM is inside the greenhouse's forward bay (eyePoints.test.ts).

stores.source: One rack INSIDE the fuselage hull on the centerline under the wing center section, its lug at x -0.9 m, y -0.53 m, so the mk13 mesh (4.09 m long, bottom 0.60 m below its lug) stays inside the drawn hull (tests/tools/models/internalBay.test.ts) and inside the bay doors' 4.3 m (x -3.3 to 1.0 m); the position is an ESTIMATE. It releases only through the bay doors (C2). HISTORIC LOAD: one Mark 13 torpedo, or one 2,000 lb bomb, or four 500 lb bombs, in the bay (EN-WP); rockets on wing rails are not modeled. MODELED (D1 plan D7 and D8, Mark, 2026-10-09): one Mk 13. The store, mk13, is the 1944 Mk 13 with its shroud ring and drag ring, given the Mod 10's figures: 1,005 kg (2,216 lb) all-up and 274 kg (603 lb) of TNT, SOURCED (NavWeaps, 'United States of America Torpedoes of World War II', read 2026-10-09); 33.5 knots (17.23 m/s) for 3,660 m (4,000 yd), SOURCED (same). DROP ENVELOPE: at most 410 knots (210.9 m/s) and 2,400 ft (730 m), SOURCED (same: the recommended maximum once the drag and shroud rings were fitted, in general use by the fall of 1944). Forgiving, as Mark asked: the early Mk 13's 50 ft and 110 knots is not used. RUN: the exploder arms after 180 m (200 yd) of water travel, SOURCED (same); depth 3 m (10 ft) is an ESTIMATE (it could be set to as much as 15 m, same). DERIVED from the fleet's AN-M65 ESTIMATES, as the Type 98's were: drag area 0.132 m2 by frontal area (22.4 in = 0.569 m against the AN-M65's 0.47 m), dragPerM 1.32e-5 by frontal area over mass, damage 136 by explosive (274 / 240.9 x 120), blast radius 31 m by the cube root of the explosive. lifetimeS 60 covers the fall. The torpedo's mass and drag are added to emptyKg by storesSpec, so the loaded airplane is above the graded card's testMassKg; the cards are graded clean.
